provenance.brief: benchmarks/briefs/social-messenger.md (Milestones section, acceptance checklists; Executors and Statuses paragraphs)
provenance.phase: LLP 0201 P2 hardening — DRAFT until the P3 freeze pins hashes
provenance.note: Every numbered acceptance checklist item of M1-M8 is split into atomic assertions, one per observable clause, per the brief's Executors paragraph ('every assertion (not merely every numbered item - compound items get one class per clause) is assigned exactly one executor class'). IDs are stable from P1 forward; the P3 freeze may add assertions but never renumbers existing ones. P2 marks M6 simulator assertions greenRequired:false because their lane-native artifact is recorded and scored separately from web authoring green. M8 was added by LLP 0201's 2026-08-11 dated amendment (additive; prior records record M8 not-run).

executorClasses.suite-required: The builder's scripted acceptance suite must cover it; the harness validates a coverage manifest mapping every suite-required assertion to a test. Green requires a passing coverage-validated suite run.
executorClasses.choreo: Two-client web behavior executed by the choreography harness, plus M6 simulator behavior recorded through a separate lane-native artifact. A milestone's green receipt requires its web choreography segment; assertions explicitly marked greenRequired:false remain separately scored evidence.
executorClasses.grader: Source inspection, API probing, snapshot comparison - grader phase only; never gates the milestone's green receipt.

runScopeValues.all: Asserted whenever the milestone is in the run's scope (reduced = M1-M3, full = M1-M8).
runScopeValues.full-only: Asserted on full runs only, even though the milestone is also in reduced scope (the brief marks these explicitly).

assertions.text: Sign up as a new user with email + password (password >= 8 chars) succeeds.
After signup the app lands in the authenticated state.
Signing up with a duplicate handle is rejected with a visible error.
Signing up with a duplicate email is rejected with a visible error.
Kill and relaunch the app; the session persists (still signed in).
assertions.notes: App kill/relaunch is client-lifecycle behavior driven by the harness choreography script, not the scripted suite.

assertions.text: Log out, relaunch: the app is signed out.
After logout the old session token no longer works against the backend (server-side revocation, verified via the API).
assertions.notes: The brief marks this API sub-assertion run-scope-conditional: [grader] via the API on full runs only.

assertions.text: Editing display name and bio persists (updated values shown on own profile).
Display-name and bio edits are visible on the other client without manual refresh.
Uploading a fixture avatar succeeds.
The uploaded avatar renders on the profile (avatars beside posts and messages are asserted at M2/M3, where those surfaces exist).

Source inspection: passwords are stored via built-in auth or a named adaptive KDF (argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt at standard published parameters); a managed auth provider qualifies by its documentation, with the grader verifying the lane uses the documented provider path, not provider internals.
No plaintext or reversible password storage in server persistence, client bundles, or logs (the fixture pack's credential files are a declared test-fixture exception - they live outside the app).
Create a text post.
Create an image post with 2 fixture images.
Create a video post.
All three created posts render in the Global feed on the other client without manual refresh.
Feed items render with the author's avatar and display name.
Bob follows Alice; Alice's posts appear in Bob's Following feed.
Alice's follower count updates live when Bob follows her.
After Bob unfollows, on next feed load Alice's posts (including older ones) no longer appear in his Following feed.
After the unfollow, Alice's posts remain visible in the Global feed (unfollow is projection-scoped, not content revocation).
A post from a user Bob doesn't follow appears in his Global feed.
That same post is absent from Bob's Following feed.
An http(s) URL in a text post renders as tappable text opening the system browser.
No preview card renders for the URL (no unfurling).
Like from client B; the like count updates live on client A.
Unlike works: the like is cleared and the count decrements (idempotent set-state toggle).
Repost from client B; feeds show the repost attributed 'reposted by {display name}'.
Reposting again removes the repost (toggle).
A repost by a followed user surfaces the original author's post in the Following feed.
Reply to a post; the parent's reply count increments live.
The thread screen shows the parent and its direct replies in chronological order.
The reply is absent from both feeds (replies appear only on thread screens).
With >20 seeded posts, scrolling loads the next page (20 per page) in the Following tab.
With >20 seeded posts, scrolling loads the next page in the Global tab.
Feed pagination produces no duplicates and no gaps across pages in either tab.
With no explicit self-follow edge, Bob's own original posts remain in his Following feed, including when he follows no other accounts.
With no explicit self-follow edge, Bob's own reposts remain in his Following feed.
Implicit self-follow feed membership does not change Bob's follower or following counts.
Alice DMs Bob and Bob replies; both clients see the messages live.
DM messages render with sender avatars.
Starting the 'same' DM again reuses the existing channel (at most one DM channel per user pair).
Create a group with Alice, Bob, and Carol.
A second group with the same three members coexists as a distinct group.
Bob types; Alice sees the '…' typing indicator within 2 s.
The typing indicator expires within 5 s of Bob's last keystroke.
Receipt ticks transition sent -> delivered -> read, monotonically, as Bob's client fetches and then opens the conversation.
The group aggregate indicator shows a state only when every member of the message's recipient set (membership at send time) has reached it - it waits for the slowest member.
A quoted reply renders the quoted excerpt in its bubble.
Tapping the quoted excerpt scrolls/jumps to the original message.
assertions.notes: Single-client UI interaction: suite-covered (web automation), not two-client choreography.

assertions.text: Admin removes Carol; she immediately stops receiving new messages.
The removed member still sees her local copy of pre-removal history.
assertions.notes: Client-local retention observed on the removed member's client.

assertions.text: A non-admin cannot remove members.
The seed is idempotent: a second run produces no duplicates - judged per installed segment, covering every starter-log segment installed so far (each milestone's suite re-runs this).
Photo message end-to-end: Alice picks a fixture image and sends it as a message.
Bob sees the photo rendered inline from a query result (not a placeholder), live.
Video message end-to-end: a fixture video sends as a message.
The video message plays on the recipient.
Bob reacts 👍; Alice sees the reaction live.
Bob switches to ❤️: the new emoji replaces the previous one (at most one reaction per user per message).
Bob taps ❤️ again: the reaction is removed.
Alice edits a sent message within the window; Bob sees the new text live.
The edited bubble shows an 'edited' label.
Under the shortened-windows config, an edit attempted after the window is rejected server-side (verified via the API, not just the absence of the UI affordance).
Alice deletes a message (delete-for-everyone); Bob sees the 'This message was deleted' tombstone.
After the delete, the media URL no longer serves the asset.
Set a DM to disappearing (shortened-windows config): with both clients closed at expiry, the server refuses the expired message (API check).
assertions.notes: Checklist item 1 is tagged [grader] in the brief; all three of its clauses grade in the grader phase.

assertions.text: Each client purges the expired message on next launch/reconnect (connected: within tolerance; disconnected: immediately on reconnect).
assertions.notes: Grader-verified via web automation per the item's [grader] tag.

assertions.text: The expired message no longer appears in offline search after the client has synced the expiry.
View-once photo: Bob can open it exactly once (first open works).
Bob's second open of the view-once photo is denied.
A direct asset fetch after the view is refused server-side.
Admin sets the group accent color and background; Carol sees both (customization synced to all members).
A non-admin cannot rename the group.
People search finds 'car' -> Carol (case-insensitive word-prefix matching).
In-chat search finds a known seeded string.
Global message search groups results by chat.
Warm-offline: with the app running, connectivity cut, search over previously synced messages still returns results (no restart - cold-start offline search is verified at M6).

M6.title: Offline writes, push seam, custom-client API

assertions.text: Cold-start offline (iOS simulator, backend stopped): previously synced chats and message history render.
Cold-start offline: previously viewed media renders.
Cold-start offline: search over synced messages works.
Cold-start offline: a previously viewed view-once photo does NOT render (view-once media is never durably cached).
Two messages composed offline both show a visible pending state.
On reconnect the queued messages flush and arrive in order.
The flushed messages walk the normal receipt states and reach 'read'.

With Bob's clients closed, Alice messages him: the backend logs a push payload with the correct targetUserId, chatId, senderDisplayName, and preview (first 80 chars of text, or 'Photo'/'Video' for media).
A view-once photo previews as 'Photo' in the logged push payload.
scripts/custom-client-demo.mjs runs green against the live backend from a clean checkout.

The demo script exercises every listed API operation: authenticate (or use an issued token), list conversations, page through message history, send a text message, and receive new messages (streaming or documented polling).
Grader-written variation: following only API.md, fetch the latest message of a named conversation (documentation quality is part of the bar).

The scale-replay adapter passes the fixture pack's action-schema conformance check: it replays a 50-action sample log green, harness-validated, on the dev instance (adapter authoring is inside M6's coverage manifest, cap, and authoring clock).
assertions.notes: The brief places this inside M6's coverage manifest (hence suite-required) while the pass receipt is harness-validated; see the manifest README's ambiguity log.

M7.title: Day-2 evolution (fresh session, after M1-M6 grading)

assertions.text: Create a poll in a group: question (<=200 chars) with 2-4 options (<=50 chars each).
Members vote; live tallies update on all members' clients.
Changing a vote adjusts the counts (one vote per user, changeable).
A duplicate/retried vote intent does not flip state (idempotent set-state per the global ruling).
An offline vote queues and settles on reconnect.
Message counts are correct for pre-existing conversations (backfill): currently visible messages, excluding tombstoned and expired messages; polls count as messages.
Message counts increment with new messages (maintained forward), shown in chat settings.
Pre-existing messages, media, receipts, and reactions are intact after the migration, compared against the pre-M7 snapshot exported through the custom-client API over the M6 field manifest.
The acceptance suites of previously-green milestones still pass (prior failures are preserved, not repaired under M7's budget).
assertions.notes: Conditional per the brief's DAG note: the regression item applies only to milestones that were green before M7; prior failures are preserved.

assertions.text: Alice's Insights screen shows the six lifetime totals (posts, likes received, reposts received, replies received, followers, following) matching the seeded content.
After Bob likes one of Alice's posts, a refresh of Alice's Insights increments her likes-received total.
The 7-day activity breakdown buckets a post created today under today (server-time UTC day boundaries).
Days with no activity render as zero, not omitted.
Trending ranks the post with the most likes in the trailing 24 h first.
An older heavily-liked post (>24 h) is absent from Trending.
A like-count tie in Trending breaks newest-first.

Under the shortened digest config with every client closed, seeded activity produces exactly one logged digest payload per active user, with correct newFollowers, newPostsInFollowing, unreadMessages, and unreadChats counts.
A persona with no activity in the period receives no digest.
A following period with no new activity emits no digest.
A backend restart mid-period does not double-emit any user's digest (exactly one digest per user per period).
Activity in a chat the target user is not a member of never contributes to that user's digest counts.
With Alice signed in on two clients, a message sent on client 1 appears on client 2 live.
Opening the conversation on client 1 clears the unread indication on client 2 (cross-device read state).
With both of Alice's clients warm-offline, each composes one message in the same chat; on reconnect both settle in server-arrival order with no loss and no duplicates.
After the dual-offline reconnect the flushed messages' receipts advance normally.
Compose offline; kill and relaunch the app still offline: the queued messages render as pending (the offline queue is durable across restart).
On reconnect after the offline restart, the queued messages flush in order and reach 'read' normally.
